sentence: This project builds deep-learning tools that align MRI scans taken over time to measure changes linked to Alzheimer's disease.
This project provides microscopes and other equipment to image and assess the function of living cells and animal models.
This project builds a microfluidic device that isolates and expands rare immune cells from a patient's blood to treat ovarian cancer.
This project studies how the brain and the heart interact in larval zebrafish by building a complete map of their connections.
This project builds a liquid biopsy approach that measures cells in blood to predict how lung cancer patients respond to immunotherapy.
This project develops MRI tools that image vascular stiffness and flow to study how vascular disease is involved in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how losing one gene changes mitochondria in mouse models and human organoids of pancreatic cystic neoplasms.
This project studies how regions of the human genome linked to coronary artery disease work to contribute to the disease.
This project studies the genomes of a rhesus macaque colony to plan breeding that keeps genetic diversity for AIDS researchers.
This project studies what signals make a type of T cell drive deadly graft-versus-host disease while keeping immunity against cancer.
This project tests whether sulindac helps colorectal cancer respond better to immunotherapy.
This project studies how to prevent necrotizing enterocolitis, a disease where tissue in the small or large intestine is injured.
This project studies how changes in conformational dynamics weaken the activity of human enzymes linked to disease.
This project builds a system from human thalamic and cortical organoids that reproduces a human brain wave called corticothalamic oscillation.
This project studies how rectal cancer responds early to radiation and immunotherapy by examining biopsy tissue at molecular, cellular and spatial levels.
This project builds a handheld optical coherence tomography system for retinal exams of non-sedated neonates screened for retinopathy of prematurity.
This project studies whether toxic amyloid-beta and tau proteins made in response to severe pneumonia cause neurological and organ damage during extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.
This project builds a tool that changes the rate of genetic variation in specific regions of the genome to study effects on gene regulation.
